executive_view.headline: Across 4,203 stays over 12 months, the dataset shows a 9.0% all-cause 30-day readmission rate, a 2.4% in-hospital mortality rate, and an average length of stay of 3.72 days, with Cardiology generating the highest total charges of any department.

paragraphs.text: The dataset covers 4,203 inpatient stays across 1,707 patients and 3,455 discharges, with total charges ranging widely from $3,500.23 to $827,622.78 per stay.
Total charges fell sharply in Oct 2026 compared with Sep 2026, which warrants attention given the 12-month window and possible seasonal patterns.

findings.text: Cardiology accounts for the largest share of total charges at $41,663,189.13, followed by Orthopedics at $33,207,578.70, while Neurology is the lowest among named departments at $14,422,030.35.
Total charges are highly skewed: the median stay costs $22,216.05 but the mean is $32,105.12, pulled upward by outlier stays reaching $827,622.78, which have been flagged but kept in the data.
Total charges dropped in Oct 2026 versus Sep 2026; because the data covers only 12 months with no prior-year comparison, it is not possible to determine whether this is seasonal or a genuine decline.
The 30-day readmission rate of 9.0% is all-cause and includes planned readmissions, so the figure likely overstates avoidable readmissions; rates are also crude and not risk-adjusted.
